cases.sentence: Толь прочел ее Ермолову, предлагая ему заняться ___.
cases.explain: «дальнейшими распоряжениями» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: On the morning of the fourth of October Kutúzov signed the dispositions. Toll read them to Ermólov, asking him to attend to the further arrangements.

cases.sentence: «Die erste Colonne marschirt[940] ___ идет туда-то и туда-то, die zweite Colonne marschirt[941] вторая колонна идет туда-то и туда-то,» и т. д.
cases.explain: «Первая колонна» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “The First Column will march here and here,” “the Second Column will march there and there,” and so on; and on paper, all these columns arrived at their places at the appointed time and destroyed the enemy. Everything had been admirably thought out as is usual in dispositions, and as is always the case, not a single column reached its place at the appointed time.

cases.sentence: «Die erste Colonne marschirt[940] Первая колонна идет туда-то и туда-то, die zweite Colonne marschirt[941] ___ идет туда-то и туда-то,» и т. д.
cases.explain: «вторая колонна» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: Когда диспозиция была готова в ___ экземпляров, был призван офицер и послан к Ермолову, чтобы передать ему бумаги для исполнения.
cases.explain: «должном количестве» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: When the necessary number of copies of the dispositions had been prepared, an officer was summoned and sent to deliver them to Ermólov to deal with. A young officer of the Horse Guards, Kutúzov’s orderly, pleased at the importance of the mission entrusted to him, went to Ermólov’s quarters.

cases.sentence: ___ пошел к генералу, у которого часто бывал Ермолов.
cases.explain: «Кавалергардский офицер» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Gone away,” said Ermólov’s orderly. The officer of the Horse Guards went to a general with whom Ermólov was often to be found.

cases.explain: «Кавалергардский офицер» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The officer, mounting his horse, rode off to someone else.

cases.sentence: Кто говорил, что видели, как Ермолов проехал с ___ куда-то, кто говорил, что он верно опять дома.
cases.explain: «другими генералами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “If only they don’t make me responsible for this delay! What a nuisance it is!” thought the officer, and he rode round the whole camp. One man said he had seen Ermólov ride past with some other generals, others said he must have returned home. The officer searched till six o’clock in the evening without even stopping to eat. Ermólov was nowhere to be found and no one knew where he was. The officer snatched a little food at a comrade’s, and rode again to the vanguard to find Milorádovich. Milorádovich too was away, but here he was told that he had gone to a ball at General Kíkin’s and that Ermólov was probably there too.

cases.sentence: — А вон, в Ечкине, — сказал ___, указывая на далекий, помещичий дом.
cases.explain: «казачий офицер» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Why, there, over at Échkino,” said a Cossack officer, pointing to a country house in the far distance.

cases.sentence: Издалека еще, подъезжая к дому, он услыхал дружные, веселые звуки плясовой ___.
cases.explain: «солдатской песни» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The officer rode out beyond our lines to Échkino. While still at a distance he heard as he rode the merry sounds of a soldier’s dance song proceeding from the house.

cases.sentence: Офицера ввели в дверь, и он увидал вдруг всех вместе ___ армии, в том числе и большую, заметную фигуру Ермолова.
cases.explain: «важных генералов» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “In the meadows … in the meadows!” he heard, accompanied by whistling and the sound of a torban, drowned every now and then by shouts. These sounds made his spirits rise, but at the same time he was afraid that he would be blamed for not having executed sooner the important order entrusted to him. It was already past eight o’clock. He dismounted and went up into the porch of a large country house which had remained intact between the Russian and French forces. In the refreshment room and the hall, footmen were bustling about with wine and viands. Groups of singers stood outside the windows. The officer was admitted and immediately saw all the chief generals of the army together, and among them Ermólov’s big imposing figure. They all had their coats unbuttoned and were standing in a semicircle with flushed and animated faces, laughing loudly. In the middle of the room a short handsome general with a red face was dancing the trepák with much spirit and agility.

cases.sentence: В середине залы, красивый, невысокий генерал с ___ бойко и ловко выделывал трепака.
cases.explain: «красным лицом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.

cases.sentence: Офицер чувствовал, что, входя в эту минуту с ___, он делается вдвойне виноват, и он хотел подождать; но один из генералов увидал его и, узнав зачем он, сказал Ермолову.
cases.explain: «важным приказанием» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: The officer felt that by arriving with important orders at such a moment he was doubly to blame, and he would have preferred to wait; but one of the generals espied him and, hearing what he had come about, informed Ermólov. Ermólov came forward with a frown on his face and, hearing what the officer had to say, took the papers from him without a word.
